lesson.title: 4.4 Is there a TV in the bedroom?
lesson.unit_title: Life at home, every day and yesterday
lesson.unit_outcome: Say where people and things are at home, talk about the lights and machines, ask what there is, describe someone's morning in order, say what you did yesterday and on which day, ask and tell the time, say how often you do things and give dates.
lesson.lesson_title: Is there a TV in the bedroom?
lesson.sub_lesson_title: Is there a TV in the bedroom?
lesson.goal: Ask whether something is in a room with Is there…? / Are there…?, answer with short answers, and ask How many … are there? (Is there a TV in the bedroom? No, there isn't.).
lesson.grammar_function: A follow-up of A1 4.4 There Is and There Are: A1 says there is and there are; A1+ 4.4 asks with them. The one new grammar relationship is the question with be before there (Is there a lamp in the living room? / Are there two chairs in the dining room?) and its short answers (Yes, there is. / No, there isn't. / Yes, there are. / No, there aren't.), with How many … are there? for counting. A1 4.4's room photos answer the questions, and a No answer is only asked about a photo that plainly does not show the thing (no TV and no computer in A1's bedroom; three books, not four). A1+ 2.9's buses, men and women come back with How many … are there?. A negative sentence is never set against a photo in a picture bank.
lesson.prerequisite: A1 4.4 there is and there are; A1 4.1-4.3 rooms and places; A1+ 2.9 buses, men, women; A1+ 3.4 short answers.
lesson.speaking_outcome: Link is there (IZ-ther) and are there (AR-ther); stress the not in isn't and aren't. Do not require native-like speed.
